annotations.title: Government contract prices (what public buyers paid)

description: Use this when a user asks what governments, councils, hospitals or other public buyers actually paid for something (laptops, school meals, road resurfacing, office cleaning, electricity, ambulances, waste collection and similar purchases) in Australia (federal contracts, AusTender), Canada (federal contracts, CanadaBuys), Colombia (public contracts, SECOP II), EU and EEA states (TED), France (public contracts, DECP), the United Kingdom (Contracts Finder), New Zealand (GETS), Singapore (GeBIZ), the United States (federal contracts) or South Africa (public contracts, eTenders). Returns, from official contract award notices, the median awarded value per contract, a typical range (10th–90th percentile), the number of awards, the period covered, a confidence label, and the official source and licence. Important: the figures are TOTAL values per contract (lot), not unit prices, unless the answer states a unit price (only when the notices give a quantity and unit). Nothing is returned for fewer than 5 awards, and individual suppliers are never named. How fresh: Australia (federal contracts, AusTender) and the United Kingdom (Contracts Finder): continuous: buyers publish award notices after a contract is awarded; Canada (federal contracts, CanadaBuys): daily: CanadaBuys refreshes the award notice files every day and our copy is collected once a day; Colombia (public contracts, SECOP II): daily: Colombia Compra Eficiente refreshes the open dataset about daily and our copy is collected once a day; EU and EEA states (TED): daily on working days: notices appear on TED within days of the buyer sending them; France (public contracts, DECP): daily: the consolidated monthly files are refreshed about daily and our copy is collected once a day; New Zealand (GETS): quarterly; awards up to the end of the last quarter; Singapore (GeBIZ): yearly; the United States (federal contracts): daily: agencies report contract actions within days and USAspending refreshes nightly; South Africa (public contracts, eTenders): monthly: the Open Contracting Partnership refreshes the eTenders bulk file about once a month and our copy is collected once a day. Do not use for what consumers or private companies pay, for tenders that are still open (those carry estimates, not prices paid), for the contracts of one named supplier, for asking prices, or for other countries.

buyer_area.description: Optional region or city to narrow to, see the country notes below. AU: part of a federal agency's name ('Defence', 'Health', 'Parliamentary Services'); contracts have no delivery place. CA: not used; all federal buyers are summarised together. CO: not used; all public buyers are summarised together. EU and EEA: the buyer's city, as written on the notice (e.g. 'Lyon', 'München'). FR: not used; all French public buyers are summarised together. GB: a region ('London', 'North West', 'Scotland', 'Wales', 'Yorkshire and The Humber' ...); nationwide contracts that list the region are included. NZ: part of the posting agency's name ('Auckland Council', 'Waka Kotahi', 'Health'); needs at least 5 awards. SG: part of an agency name ('National Library Board', 'Health Sciences Authority'). US: a state name or code ('Virginia', 'VA'); filters by where the work is done. ZA: not used; all public buyers are summarised together.

country.description: AU = Australia (AusTender federal contract notices); CA = Canada (federal award notices on CanadaBuys); CO = Colombia (signed public contracts in SECOP II); EU and EEA states, by the country of the public buyer, as ISO codes: AT = Austria, BE = Belgium, BG = Bulgaria, HR = Croatia, CY = Cyprus, CZ = Czechia, DK = Denmark, EE = Estonia, FI = Finland, FR = France, DE = Germany, GR = Greece, HU = Hungary, IE = Ireland, IT = Italy, LV = Latvia, LT = Lithuania, LU = Luxembourg, MT = Malta, NL = the Netherlands, PL = Poland, PT = Portugal, RO = Romania, SK = Slovakia, SI = Slovenia, ES = Spain, SE = Sweden, IS = Iceland, LI = Liechtenstein, NO = Norway. Award notices above the EU procurement thresholds from TED.; FR = France (awarded public contracts, DECP); GB = United Kingdom (Contracts Finder awarded contracts); NZ = New Zealand (GETS contract award notices); SG = Singapore (GeBIZ tenders); US = United States, federal agencies' contracts only (not state or local governments); ZA = South Africa (signed public contracts on the National Treasury eTenders portal)

cpv.description: Optional official product code, to be exact, where the source uses one (the country notes say which code system), e.g. the CPV code 30213100 for portable computers; a prefix such as 3021 covers the whole group. AU: a UNSPSC code or prefix of 2 to 8 digits (43211503 = notebook computers, 4321 = computers), not a CPV code. CA: not used. CO: not used. EU and EEA: an 8-digit CPV code (30213100) or a shorter prefix (3021) for a whole group; a lot counts when its own main product code is in that group. FR: a CPV code of 2 digits (a division) or 4 to 8 digits (read as the 4-digit group, e.g. 3021); used instead of the words in what. GB: a full 8-digit CPV code (45233142) instead of the keyword; only notices that list the code themselves are used. NZ: not used (New Zealand notices carry no CPV codes). SG: not used (Singapore tenders carry no CPV codes). US: a product or service code (PSC, e.g. 7010 or psc:7010) or a NAICS code (e.g. 334111 or naics:334111) instead of the keyword; there are no CPV codes in the US. ZA: not used.

months.description: How many recent months of awards to include. Default 24. AU: not used; the newest 21 days of notices are read. CA: not used; each figure covers the newest 24 months of awards. CO: not used; each figure covers the newest 12 months of signed contracts. EU and EEA: up to 60; only the newest 1,000 matching notices are read, so a very common purchase covers a shorter period than asked (the answer says so). FR: not used; each figure covers contracts notified in the newest 12 months. GB: 1 to 60 months, by award date. NZ: not used; the newest 24 months of awards are always shown. SG: 1 to 60 months by award date; the dataset covers FY2021 onwards and is updated about yearly. US: 1 to 60 months of new awards, read in up to 12 slices. ZA: not used; each figure covers the newest 24 months of signed contracts.

what.description: What was bought, in plain words: 'laptops', 'school meals', 'road resurfacing', 'office cleaning', 'electricity', 'ambulances', 'waste collection'. Common purchases are matched to official product codes; anything else is searched as free text in the award notices. AU: a word or phrase searched in the contract title and description (common purchases such as 'laptops' or 'catering' also use their UNSPSC code). Federal agencies only. CA: a common purchase in plain words ('translation services', 'legal services', 'catering', 'consultancy', 'IT services', 'laptops', 'security guards'). Recognised from the words in the notice title; other wording is not searched. CO: a common purchase in plain words ('catering', 'security guard services', 'office cleaning', 'laptops', 'ambulances', 'printers', 'photocopiers'). Recognised from the Spanish words in the contract description; other wording is not searched. EU and EEA: common purchases are matched to CPV product codes (laptops, desktop computers, school meals, road resurfacing, office cleaning, electricity, natural gas, ambulances, waste collection and about 30 more, in English and the main EU languages); anything else is a free-text search of the award notices, best in the buyer country's language. FR: a common purchase in plain words, in French or English ('ordinateurs portables', 'laptops', 'restauration scolaire', 'road resurfacing', 'office cleaning', 'ambulances'). Recognised from the contract's CPV product code. GB: a keyword or phrase searched in the award notices (common purchases such as 'laptops' or 'road resurfacing' use a tuned keyword). Several words are searched as an exact phrase, so shorter is better. NZ: optional (left out = all awards); a common purchase in plain words ('buses', 'laptops', 'cleaning', 'road resurfacing'; a purchase with fewer than 5 awards in 24 months gets no figure) or 'all'; read from the price library, not searched live. SG: a word or phrase searched in the tender description ('cleaning', 'laptops', 'security services'); common purchases use a tuned keyword. US: a phrase searched in the federal award descriptions (common purchases such as 'laptops' use a tuned keyword; 'road resurfacing' uses the road-repair product code Z2LB). Several words must appear together, so shorter is better. ZA: a common purchase in plain words ('security guard services', 'building cleaning', 'catering', 'laptops', 'office furniture', 'photocopiers'). Recognised from the words in the contract description; other wording is not searched.

name: pricepaid_contract_prices

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Official published index', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Posted or listed price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.

title: Government contract prices (what public buyers paid)
